Package com.signalwire.sdk.relay

Class Device

java.lang.Object
com.signalwire.sdk.relay.Device
public final class Device extends Object
A typed view of the RELAY {type, params} device object that recurs as a raw Map<String, Object> across Call.connect(java.util.List<java.util.List<java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>>>, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>), Call.refer(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>), RelayClient.dial(java.util.List<java.util.List<java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>>>, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, long) and Call.tap(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>).

The wire shape is fixed (extracted from switchblade's PublicCallConnectParams / PublicCallDialParams / PublicCallReferParams / PublicCallTapParams, mirrored in porting-sdk/relay-protocol/calling.*.params.json): every device is an object with a required string type discriminant and a params sub-object whose shape depends on the type (a phone carries to_number/from_number, a sip carries to/ headers, etc.). This class types the shape — the {type, params} envelope — so callers stop hand-rolling the two-key map and get an explicit constructor + accessors.

type stays a String. The discriminant is NOT schema-enumerated: the wire schema constrains it only to "type": {"type": "string"}, and the platform accepts device types the SDK may not know about. Typing it as an enum would reject valid values, so it is deliberately left open (the convention names phone/sip/ webrtc — see Constants.DEVICE_TYPE_PHONE etc. — but those are conveniences, not a closed set). params is left an arbitrary Map<String, Object> for the same reason: it is type-dependent and not a single fixed schema.

Additive — the raw-map path stays. Every method that takes a device still accepts a raw Map<String, Object>; this class is a convenience on top. toMap() produces a map that is byte-for-byte identical to the hand-written {"type": …, "params": …} (insertion order type then params, matching every existing call site), so routing a device through Device serialises exactly as the raw map does. 


 // typed:
 Device phone = Device.of("phone", Map.of(
     "to_number", "+15551112222", "from_number", "+15553334444"));
 call.connect(List.of(List.of(phone.toMap())), null);

 // raw map still works (parity):
 call.connect(List.of(List.of(Map.of(
     "type", "phone",
     "params", Map.of("to_number", "+15551112222",
                      "from_number", "+15553334444")))), null);

Python uses a bare dict for this object, so there is no reference equivalent — this is a documented Java addition.

  • Constructor Details

    • Device

      public Device(String type, Map<String,Object> params)
      Construct a device from its type discriminant and params sub-object.
      Parameters:
      type - the device type discriminant (e.g. "phone", "sip", "webrtc"); must not be null.
      params - the type-dependent params; null is treated as an empty map.

    • phone

      public static Device phone(String toNumber, String fromNumber)
      Convenience factory for the most common case — a phone device. Builds {type:"phone", params:{to_number, from_number}}.
      Parameters:
      toNumber - the destination E.164 number.
      fromNumber - the caller-ID E.164 number.
      Returns:
      a new phone Device.

    • sip

      public static Device sip(String to, String from)
      Convenience factory for a sip device. Builds {type:"sip", params:{to, from?}} (only non-null values).
      Parameters:
      to - the SIP destination URI.
      from - the SIP from URI, or null to omit.
      Returns:
      a new sip Device.

      public Map<String,Object> getParams()
      The type-dependent params sub-object (an unmodifiable view).

    • toMap

      public Map<String,Object> toMap()
      Serialise to the wire shape: a two-key map {"type": …, "params": …} with type inserted first, identical to the hand-written map every existing call site builds. The returned map is fresh and mutable (callers routinely nest it inside a devices list), and params is a defensive copy so later mutation of the returned map cannot corrupt this Device.
      Returns:
      a new {type, params} map ready to pass to connect/refer/dial/tap.
